auto closing pairs with conflicting patterns problems
```
Version: 1.33.1 (user setup)
Commit: 51b0b28134d51361cf996d2f0a1c698247aeabd8
Date: 2019-04-11T08:27:14.102Z
Electron: 3.1.6
Chrome: 66.0.3359.181
Node.js: 10.2.0
V8: 6.6.346.32
OS: Windows_NT x64 10.0.17763
```

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Create two auto closing pairs in a language configuration file,
```JSON
	"autoClosingPairs": [
		{"open": "(", "close": ")"},
		{"open": "(*", "close": "*)",  "notIn": ["string"]},
	],
```
2. trying using the two character auto closing pair, `(*` and you will get `(**))`.

On the other hand, if you remove the ending ')' from the closing '*)' you almost get normal function, except that in cases where `(` doesn't auto close with `)`, you get `(**`.

Note this condition exists in #57838, in a reference to the Structured Text Language, though it is not shown in the example on that feature request.  Reference the repository https://github.com/Serhioromano/vscode-st for some example.

I think the Auto Closing logic needs to consider when auto closing pairs might conflict with each other.  In this case, '(**)' overlaps with '()'.
I’ll check the editor’s pairing logic to pinpoint why the shorter `()` rule wins inside the longer `(**)` sequence and identify the safest conflict-resolution behavior.

steps.text:
This is a valid overlap bug, not a language-configuration mistake.

Typing `(` first inserts `()`. When `*` is then typed, the editor recognizes `(*` and inserts `*)`, but it does not remove the already auto-inserted `)`, producing `(**))`.

The correct behavior is to upgrade the existing short pair:

```text
(  →  ()  →  (*)
             ↓
           (**)
```

This needs an editor-core fix: when a newly completed multi-character opener has a shorter opener as its prefix, and that shorter pair’s closing text was auto-inserted immediately after the cursor, replace that closing text with the longer pair’s close. Configuration ordering alone cannot make this reliable.

A regression test should cover:

```json
"autoClosingPairs": [
  { "open": "(", "close": ")" },
  { "open": "(*", "close": "*)", "notIn": ["string"] }
]
```

and assert that typing `(` then `*` yields `(**)` with the cursor between the two `*` characters.
